To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
transversely polarised quarks fragment in a new way, that the new fragmentation function is a probe of chiral symmetry breaking, and that it is accessible in experiments at HERA, RHIC and the LHC.

1) A transversely polarised quark can fragment into a hadron with a non-trivial azimuthal dependence, which is sensitive to the chiral structure of the fragmentation function; 2) The transverse momentum distribution of the produced hadron is sensitive to the transverse spin structure of the fragmentation process; 3) This new spin-dependent fragmentation process can be studied in semi-inclusive deeply-inelastic scattering with transversely polarisable target and unpolarised beam, and

the fragmentation function of transversely-polarized quarks into unpolarized hadrons is sensitive to chiral symmetry breaking in QCD, and that this can be studied experimentally in semi-inclusive deeply-inelastic scattering and in hadron-hadro collisions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fragmentation of transversely-polarized quarks and gluons.
the spin structure of the nucleon.
a new spin-dependent observable in hadronic processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fragmentation process is sensitive to the spin structure of the quark, and that the fragmentation process itself is sensitive to the quark-gluon interaction.
the transverse momentum distribution of hadrons is a probe of quark transverse spin, and the new fragmentation function is a probe of spontaneous chiral symmetry breaking.
the transverse momentum distribution of hadrons is a sensitive probe for transverse spin and the fragmentation function that acts on this level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fragmentation of quarks is sensitive to their transverse spin, and that this is a probe of chiral symmetry breaking.

we have shown that transverse momentum distributions are sensitive to new spin-dependent fragmentation functions, that these new fragmentation functions have an interpretation as transverse momentum dependent distribution functions and that these new fragmentation function are sensitive to (spontaneously broken) chiral symmetry.
we are trying to understand the role of spin in fragmentation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fragmentation process can be used to probe the structure of the nucleon.
the transversely polarised quark jet is the key to understanding the transversely-polarised quark.

there is a new twist-2 fragmentation function that is sensitive to the transverse polarization of a quark and that this fragmentation function can be accessed by measuring azimuthal asymmetries in the transverse momentum distributions of hadrons in quark jets.
